Both functions in @fig-ecdf-sample-quantile-example are step functions,
so neither is one-to-one.
Each flat piece of one function
corresponds to a jump of the other:
for example, $\hat F(t) = 0.5$ for every $t \in [3, 4)$,
and $\hat Q$ jumps from 3 to 4 at $p = 0.5$.
So $\hat Q$ is a *generalized* inverse of $\hat F$,
not an inverse in the usual sense:
$\hat Q(\hat F(t)) \le t$ for every $t \ge x_{(1)}$,
with equality only at the observed values.
